==English== ===Etymology=== {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:differently|:afeq|different|-ly|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|differently}}; equivalent to {{af|en|different|-ly|id2=adverbial}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ˈdɪf.ə.ɹənt.li/|/ˈdɪf.ɹənt.li/|a=UK}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈdɪf.ɚ.ənt.li/|/ˈdɪf.ɹənt.li/|a=US}} * {{audio|en|en-us-differently.ogg|a=US}} ===Adverb=== {{en-adv}} # In a [[different]] way. #: {{usex|en|Things turned out '''differently''' from what I'd envisaged.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|year=1815|title=Critical Analysis of Recent Publications|journal=The Medical and Physical Journal|volume=34 |passage=I was (says Mr. Highmore) forcibly struck with the violence of its pulsation, so much so, that, if it had been '''differently''' situated, I should have considered it an ''aneurism'' of considerable magnitude.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1912|translator=w:Constance Garnett|author=w:Fyodor Dostoevsky|title=[[s:The Brothers Karamazov/Book IX/Chapter 3|The Brothers Karamazov]] |passage="You see, gentlemen, I couldn't bear the look of him, there was something in him ignoble, impudent, trampling on everything sacred, something sneering and irreverent, loathsome, loathsome. But now that he's dead, I feel '''differently'''."
"How do you mean?"
"I don't feel '''differently''', but I wish I hadn't hated him so."
"You feel penitent?"
"No, not penitent, don't write that. I'm not much good myself; I'm not very beautiful, so I had no right to consider him repulsive. That's what I mean. Write that down, if you like."}} ====Derived terms==== {{col2|en|differently able|differently abled}} ====Translations==== {{trans-top|in a different way}} * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Czech: * Danish: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Finnish: * French: * German: * Gothic: * Greek: * Hungarian: * Italian: * Latin: * Middle English: * Norman: * Norwegian: * Plautdietsch: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Russian: {{t+|ru|по-друго́му}} * Serbo-Croatian: * Sorbian: * Spanish: * Tocharian B: {{trans-bottom}} {{cln|en|manner adverbs}}
